description: Imagine crispy golden churros, dusted with cinnamon sugar, served alongside a rich, velvety chocolate dipping sauce. This classic Mexican dessert is a delightful treat, perfect for any celebration or a simple indulgence. Its irresistible combination of textures and flavors makes it a beloved favorite across generations.

instructions.title: Prepare the Churro Dough
instructions.text: In a medium saucepan, combine water, butter, 1 tablespoon sugar, and salt. Bring to a rolling boil over medium heat. Remove from heat and immediately add the flour, stirring vigorously with a wooden spoon until a ball of dough forms and pulls away from the sides of the pan. Continue stirring for about 1 minute to cook out some moisture.

instructions.title: Incorporate Eggs and Chill
instructions.text: Transfer the dough to a large bowl. Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition until fully incorporated and the dough is smooth and glossy. The dough should be thick enough to hold its shape. Let the dough cool slightly, about 10 minutes, so it is easier to handle.

instructions.title: Heat Oil and Prepare Piping Bag
instructions.text: Pour vegetable oil into a deep, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, to a depth of about 2-3 inches. Heat the oil over medium-high heat until it reaches 350-375F (175-190C). While the oil heats, fit a large pastry bag with a large star tip (like an Ateco 826 or 827) and fill it with the churro dough.

instructions.title: Fry the Churros
instructions.text: Carefully pipe 4-6 inch strips of dough directly into the hot oil, using kitchen shears or a knife to cut the dough. Do not overcrowd the pot. Fry for 2-3 minutes per side, or until golden brown and cooked through. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the fried churros to a plate lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.

instructions.title: Coat with Cinnamon Sugar
instructions.text: While the churros are still warm, combine 1/2 cup granulated sugar and ground cinnamon in a shallow dish. Roll the churros in the cinnamon sugar mixture until evenly coated. Set aside on a serving platter.

instructions.title: Make the Chocolate Sauce and Serve
instructions.text: In a small saucepan, heat heavy cream over medium heat until it just begins to simmer. Remove from heat and add the chopped dark chocolate, powdered sugar (if using), and vanilla extract (if using). Stir until the chocolate is completely melted and the sauce is smooth and glossy. Serve the warm churros immediately with the rich chocolate dipping sauce.

tips: To achieve perfectly crispy churros, ensure your oil temperature stays consistent. If it drops too low, the churros will absorb too much oil and become greasy.
For an extra layer of flavor in your chocolate sauce, you can add a pinch of cayenne pepper or a splash of Kahlua for a grown-up twist.
Churros are best enjoyed fresh, right after frying. If you have leftovers, reheat them briefly in an oven or air fryer to regain some crispiness.
